claims.text: High configurational entropy in high-entropy alloys arises from the random distribution of multiple atomic species.
High configurational entropy stabilizes superconductivity by homogenizing electron-phonon interactions and local pairing potentials.
High configurational entropy produces a superconducting transition temperature that is robust against external pressure.
The candidate material is a random solid solution containing at least five elements and may have a CsCl-type structure similar to MTe systems.
AgInSnPbBiTe5 exhibits an almost pressure-independent Tc between 13.0 and 35.1 GPa.
High configurational entropy leads to spatially homogeneous electron-phonon coupling and pairing potentials across the disordered lattice.
Homogenized electron-phonon interactions reduce sensitivity to lattice distortions and pressure.
Lower-entropy or ordered systems generally show larger changes in Tc under small perturbations.
When the relevant MTe phases have a CsCl-type structure, they are superconducting under high pressure.
The uncharacterized candidate high-entropy alloy will exhibit a superconducting transition under pressure at low temperature.
The candidate alloy's Tc will remain nearly constant over the tested pressure range.
The candidate alloy will have a spatially homogeneous superconducting gap.
Lower-entropy analogues will exhibit greater pressure sensitivity of Tc than the high-entropy candidate.
The proposed entropy-based mechanism should apply up to approximately 35 GPa while configurational entropy remains high.
Extreme pressure or significant compositional ordering may cause superconducting behavior different from the proposed robust response.
The microscopic electron-phonon mechanism and the minimum mixing entropy required for robust superconductivity remain unresolved in the candidate alloy.
A reduced-entropy derivative tested under the same pressure and temperature conditions provides a controlled comparison for isolating the effect of configurational entropy.
Failure to observe a near-constant Tc and uniform gap, or failure to observe a difference from the reduced-entropy control, would falsify the proposed entropy-stabilization hypothesis.
